Information since September points to a strong labor market and moderate growth, with weak business investment/exports and inflation below 2%. Consistent with Sims (1992), exogenous monetary easing—via a lower federal funds rate and reserve-adding T-bill purchases/repos—should modestly lift real activity and support policy transmission. In an inflation-targeting framework à la Svensson, easing is appropriate when inflation and longer-term expectations (as surveyed by Bullard) run below target. The coexistence of low unemployment and muted inflation is also compatible with sticky prices/wages noted in the literature (e.g., Christiano and Eichenbaum), supporting a cautiously positive but not exuberant outlook.
